title: Precision Profile Activator: Canary & Telemetry Probes for E4M3/E5M2 FP8 Enablement
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Enable an automated, telemetry-driven canary (the 'Precision Profile Activator') to safely flip FP8 profiles (E4M3/E5M2) on Hopper-class GPUs. This ticket scopes the canary mechanics, telemetry hunting rules, calibration refactors, and the guardrails that will prevent silent regressions to model quality or tail latency. The goal is to create a small, repeatable activation workflow that surfaces accuracy drift early and provides deterministic rollback and fallback to INT8 or FP16 model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Canary path can be triggered via API and config (canary_id) and target a specific model version + quant profile.
Telemetry rules detect accuracy regressions with >95% precision on our golden prompt set within 30 minutes of canary traffic.
Automatic circuit-breaker triggers and rollbacks (to INT8/FP16) are validated in staging with two different model families and at least one real-customer workload replay.
End-to-end calibration run completes within SLOs (95th percentile < 10 minutes) and produces reproducible scale/zero-point artifacts.
All alerts and dashboards are in place: canary health, token-level cost delta, P95 latency delta, output-perplexity delta, and embedding drift gauge.
Design doc and safety checklist reviewed and approved by Product and Security.
Automated smoke tests in CI that simulate per-op overflow and quant-fallback are green.
steps: Design final canary activation API and config flags (feature gate: quant.activator.enabled).
Refactor calibration pipeline to expose per-layer statistics and deterministic seeds for reproducibility.
Implement telemetry hunter: short-window probes to compute model output drift (LLR, token-loss delta, embedding cosine similarity) and latency percentiles.
Create canary orchestration: shadow -> 0.5% live traffic -> 5% -> 20% with hold windows and automated gating.
Add rollback hooks that fall back to INT8/FP16 variant and surface PRs for manual triage.
Run calibration & accuracy validation across two representative models (LlamaX-13B compat model, Redmond-7B) and three prompt suites (general convo, code, embeddings).
Add dashboards + runbooks, and schedule a safety review with Security + Product.
telemetry_signals: perplexity increase on held-out eval set
embedding cosine similarity drop (avg and 5th percentile)
ratio of requests hitting fallback variant
rollout_plan: Internal: run activation in internal staging with synthetic traffic and assert telemetry thresholds.
Shadow: run FP8 profile in shadow mode on 2% of requests for 48 hours; collect detailed diffs and calibration logs.
Canary-1: enable 0.5% live traffic for 6 hours; require no signal breach and human review.
Canary-2: increase to 5% for 24 hours; automated gating allowed if telemetry stable.
Ramp: 20% for 48 hours with continuous monitoring; if stable, schedule full enablement with progressive autoscale.
Fallback: immediate auto-fallback to INT8/FP16 on circuit-breaker breach with incident created and on-call notified.
Post-mortem: if rollback occurs, gather calibration artifacts, golden prompt diffs, and scheduler traces for repro.
validation_results: 2026-02-21: initial synthetic calibration run (LlamaX-13B) produced -0.8% avg token-likelihood change vs FP16; further per-layer clipping required.
2026-02-28: embedding drift test on Embedding-eval (2k queries) showed mean cosine 0.997 -> pass threshold, but 2% of queries had >0.02 drop; flagged for targeted per-layer re-calibration.
2026-03-05: latency microbench on Hopper e4m3 selected profile shows 7% P95 improvement vs FP16; no OOMs in 24h stress run.
2026-03-10: dry-run canary in internal staging tripped a saturation alert on attention_out layer for one model; implemented layer-level hysteresis and retry throttles.

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive hysteresis reduces false positives but increases risk of delayed detection. We will tune thresholds with live traffic samples.
Decision: use golden prompt set + embedding probe as primary gates; token-likelihood delta used for secondary validation to reduce noise from prompt engineering.
Follow-ups: create an autoscaler safety window to avoid scale-induced tail latency during ramp phases.
Related tickets: coordinate with infra autoscaling team for GPU warmup behavior (ENG-31247).
